Cyber Attack Disrupts Brazil’s Tourism Industry, Halts Bookings and Operations

A major cyber attack targeting Brazil’s tourism industry has disrupted bookings, reservations, and daily operations at several leading travel companies, as the sector grapples with ongoing IT outages. The attack, identified as a ransomware incident, began early Monday and has affected online and internal systems at multiple firms, including travel agencies, tour operators, and ticketing services. As of Wednesday afternoon, the incident remains unresolved, with restoration efforts ongoing.

Among the industry players affected are ViagemSul, a prominent tour operator, and RoteiroBrasil, a major travel booking platform. Both have reported to the Brazilian Association of Tourism Companies (ABETUR) that their booking portals and customer management systems remain offline. "We are unable to process new reservations or access client itineraries at this time," said Ana Souza, spokesperson for ViagemSul. "Our teams are working around the clock with cybersecurity experts to restore services and secure customer data."

Industry sources indicate that the attack has forced firms to suspend online sales, cancel scheduled tours, and close customer service centers in several cities, including Rio de Janeiro, Salvador, and Foz do Iguaçu. ABETUR estimates that more than 1,200 tourism workers have been temporarily idled due to system outages. “Employees whose roles depend on IT access, such as reservation agents and itinerary planners, are unable to work,” said ABETUR president Lucas Ferreira. “We are advising companies to maintain payroll and provide support until systems are restored.”

The attack comes as Brazil’s tourism industry enters the peak June travel season, raising concerns about lost revenue and reputational impact. Analysts at Consultoria Destino estimate the sector could see a 40% drop in bookings this week if disruptions persist. “This is a critical period for domestic and international tourism,” said senior analyst Helena Prado. “Prolonged outages could erase months of recovery gains since the pandemic.”

While no customer data breaches have been confirmed, companies have urged travelers to monitor accounts for suspicious activity. The National Tourism Authority said it is assisting firms and has advised travelers to delay new bookings until systems are secure. As response teams continue to address the incident, the industry faces mounting pressure to restore confidence and resume normal operations.
